title: Many Americans 'Work Remotely' from the Office
paragraphs: Many companies in the US have asked their workers to come back to the office. But a new study shows that being in the office does not always mean working with other people face to face.

The study was done by researchers from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and the University of Virginia. In September, they asked 1,835 American workers with college degrees about their most recent day at the office.

The results were surprising. Almost half of the workers, 48.8%, said they did not have a single in-person meeting on that day. And 70.6% said at least one of their teammates was not in the office on the days they went in.

Even more surprising, 37% of the workers said they had at least one online meeting where everyone was in the same office building. In other words, people traveled to the office and then talked to each other through their computer screens.
The researchers call this "in-office remote work." They wrote that days in the office "often lack human contact," and that a very large share of workers experience this kind of work.

There are several reasons for this. Teams are often in the office on different days. Some workers do not follow their company's office rules, and some companies do not check whether workers follow them.

The researchers say that if companies want workers to get the benefits of being together, they need to make sure team members come in on the same days. Otherwise, workers may travel to the office only to have the same video calls they could have had at home.
